::: {.callout-note}
## This post is a template and is never published

The line `draft: true` in the header keeps it off the live site. To write a new post, follow the steps in README.md: make a new folder in `posts`, copy this file into it, and replace the text.
:::

## The header

The block at the very top of this file, between the two lines of three dashes, is the header. The `title` and `description` appear on the post and in the lists of writing. The `date` decides the order. The `categories` are the topics readers can choose on the Writing page; use the same spelling every time so a topic collects all its posts. When a post is ready, delete the line `draft: true`.

## Citations

A citation is the key of a reference from the file `references.bib`, inside square brackets with an @ sign. A plain citation looks like this [@ostrom1990governing], and one with a page number like this [@ostrom1990governing, p. 90]. Your MA thesis is in the file as a second example [@hojgaard2019prefiguration]. Quarto formats each citation and builds the reference list at the end of the post automatically.

To add a reference, paste its BibTeX entry into `references.bib`. Zotero can export BibTeX, and most journal pages offer it under "Cite" or "Export citation".

## Notes in the margin {#margin-notes}

A footnote is written like this.^[The footnote text goes inside the brackets. On a wide screen it appears in the margin beside the line it belongs to; on a phone it appears below the paragraph.]

## A chart from data

The chart below is drawn by a few lines of Python from the file `data.csv` in this post's folder. Change the numbers in that file and the chart changes when the site is rebuilt. The figure has a label, so the text can refer to it by number: @fig-sample uses placeholder values, for layout only.

```{python}
#| label: fig-sample
#| fig-cap: "Placeholder values for layout only. Source: name the dataset and release here, for example a Eurostat dataset code and its update date."
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.style.use("../../house.mplstyle")

data = pd.read_csv("data.csv")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.4))
ax.plot(data["year"], data["value"], color="#1F7A8C", linewidth=2)

# The latest value is marked in gold: the one point the chart is about
last = data.iloc[-1]
ax.scatter([last["year"]], [last["value"]], color="#B8975A", s=40, zorder=3)
ax.annotate(f'{last["value"]:g}', (last["year"], last["value"]),
            xytext=(8, 0), textcoords="offset points", va="center")

ax.set_ylabel("Value (placeholder)")
ax.set_xticks(data["year"][::2])
plt.show()
```

To hide the code from readers, nothing extra is needed: the site settings hide it by default.
